messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on /v1/stream (shared-gpu-prod, us-west-2). p95=420ms -> 1200ms, p99=1.8s -> 9.5s. Streaming stalls observed. Count of affected streams spiked by 300% in last 5m. page: oncall-sre

maya: acked. jumping in. seeing repeated GC-ish spikes? throwing some quick checks now.

maya: top-level impact: streaming endpoints degraded across multiple tenants on shared-gpu-prod pool. probing metrics: kernel writeback and cgroup io latency up on hosts running pool-shared-03.

tony: oncall handover: i'm available. tagging me @tony. can you paste host IDs? i'll take host-level triage.

maya: hosts: gpu-host-03a, gpu-host-03b, gpu-host-03c. running iostat and dstat now.

maya: iostat snippet:
```
Device            tps    Blk_read/s    Blk_wrtn/s   Blk_read  Blk_wrtn
nvme0n1          850.00       12.34        674.21   5.6M    300M
```

maya: cgroup sensor shows blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes_recursive for tenant-42 and tenant-99 are very high. suspect noisy neighbor writing heavy checkpoints.

kai: saw a correlated pattern in our KV cache evictions: massive eviction storms coincident with spikes. tenants with big beam search jobs hugging the pool.

sara: @maya @tony estimated customer impact: two paying customers (accts: acme-ai, vectorlabs) seeing streaming stalls and reconnects. CS notified.

customer-success: we've opened tickets for acme-ai and vectorlabs, added them to incident updates. acme reports multiple 10s stalls during interactive sessions.

tony: on host gpu-host-03a: `nvidia-smi` shows GPU util ~95% and the processes are mostly from tenant-42 (long-running sampling). Also kernel io wait high.

alex: quick mitigation options: 1) throttle tenant-42 via cgroup blkio weight 2) temporarily evict tenant-42 long running jobs to maintenance pool 3) route new streaming requests from affected tenants to dedicated fallback model variant (lower memory) 4) enable aggressive KV prefix caching to reduce IO.

tony: i'm pushing a live throttle on tenant-42: running command on pool manager:
```
redwoodctl pool throttle --pool shared-gpu-prod --tenant tenant-42 --blkio-weight 100
```

maya: ack. applying now. monitoring.

incident-bot: ACTION: throttle command accepted by pool manager; change id = chg-2039. Watch for propagated effect in 30s.

maya: 45s after throttle: p99 down to 3.2s (from 9.5s). p95 stabilized ~650ms. still above SLO but improving. KV eviction rate reduced by ~60%.

nate: can we migrate tenant-42 to dedicated capacity? if they have reserved slots we can move and avoid impacting others.

sara: acme-ai is not on a dedicated contract. vectorlabs also shared. will ask CS to push for emergency dedicated slot but can't be immediate.

kai: second mitigation: bump host-level writeback limit to smooth bulk writes for checkpointing to avoid sudden bursts: writing to /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio is risky in prod but might help short-term. recommend against unless throttle insufficient.

tony: prefer tenant-level throttle + routing fallback. initiating canary routing:
```
redwoodctl route set-fallback --route /v1/stream --tenant acme-ai --fallback-model rwd-sm-quantized
```

maya: canary routing applied for acme-ai and vectorlabs. traffic split 80/20 -> fallback. watching errors.

incident-bot: METRIC_UPDATE: after throttles + fallback, p99 ~1.1s on unaffected tenants, ~1.7s for acme-ai (with fallback). streaming disconnects decreased by 85%.

sara: immediate customer-facing note: simple mitigation in place, we estimate full SLO recovery within 15-20m if noisy tenant remains throttled or migrated. CS to update tickets.

customer-success: informing customers: "We've applied temporary routing and throttles to reduce impact. We're actively moving noisy workloads off shared pool. We'll follow up once fully resolved."

tony: next steps: 1) keep tenant-42 throttled, request ops to schedule live migration to dedicated pool if available 2) run postmortem to understand why tenant-42 checkpoint IO spiked (app behavior vs misconfigured checkpointing) 3) consider autoscaling cgroup weights by detection of blkio saturation 4) evaluate per-tenant scheduling limits to prevent future eviction storms.

maya: i've collected syslogs and blkio metrics and pushed to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/4387659999/host-metrics.tar.gz

kai: adding note: KV cache eviction policy change (short-term) helped a lot. should include as mitigation recipe in runbook.

tony: any objections to marking incident as mitigated and moving to monitoring stage? need 30m of stable p99 <1.2s.

sara: +1 from CS, customers stable.

maya: no objections. i'll stay on watch for 30m then hand to eng-runtime for postmortem. handing to @tony for timeline and RCA ownership.

tony: taking RCA ownership. immediate P1 -> P2 after 30m stable check. leaving the thread for oncall rotation handoff. ping me for any regression. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. participants: maya, tony, sara, kai, alex, nate. Severity downgraded. Follow-up: RCA ticket #RCA-7492 created and assigned to tony.

maya: notes for RCA: include: tenant checkpoint frequency, periodic vs continuous writes, model quantization memory footprint (causing heavier checkpointing), KV eviction config, pool scheduling policy, telemetry gaps.

customer-success: confirm: both acme-ai and vectorlabs acknowledged temporary mitigation and will be on standby for follow-up.

tony: thanks all. closing live mitigation loop. will post postmortem link in this thread when ready."
